clue.text: Harry Kane's rage, shot being unremarkable

indicators.note: to harry is to harass or disturb, so the following letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: The England striker's frustration at a missed shot was nothing special.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like part of a name with Kane, but it is the anagram signal working on KANESRAGESHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: something described this way is mediocre, nothing to write home about.

clue.text: Not in closet, sexier clothes come from here

parts.note: openly gay people are out, not in the closet
fitter is British slang for more attractive

explanation.surface: Revealing clothes emerge from a wardrobe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closet' looks like a wardrobe, but it is the hiding place of someone not open about sexuality.
explanation.definitionFit: A description: a shop or dealer selling garments and equipment is where clothing is bought.

clue.text: Bad sort of accent British dropped

indicators.note: dropped means the named letter is left out

parts.note: a brogue is an Irish or Scottish accent

explanation.surface: A rough-sounding accent that the British gave up.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a dishonest rascal or scoundrel is a bad sort.

clue.text: Greek has an idiosyncrasy when stammering?

parts.note: the indefinite article gives A
a stammerer repeats the opening sound of the next word, so its first letter comes twice
a tic is a habitual quirk

explanation.surface: A Greek person has a speech peculiarity when stammering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when stammering' adds a stutter on the opening letter of TIC, as a stammerer says T-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Attica is the region around Athens, and its dialect and people are Greek.

clue.text: Society rebels about Republican's bombshells

indicators.note: about means the rebels go round the next letter

parts.note: to rebel is to rise up, so rebels means uprises
R is short for Republican

explanation.surface: A group of insurgents surround a Republican's startling news.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: shocking pieces of news come as great surprises.

clue.text: Grinding rock into art with this, oddly

indicators.note: to rock is to shake about, so these letters are mixed up
oddly picks the first and third letters of the word

explanation.surface: Pounding stone to make art with a tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: wearing down by friction is a grinding process.

clue.text: Elevated books exist as a source of inspiration

indicators.note: in a down entry, elevated means read upwards, backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, books of the Bible
to exist is to be, and are is a form of that

explanation.surface: Highbrow books exist to inspire readers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek Muse of love poetry, and muses are sources of artistic inspiration.

clue.text: Awfully at sea, as bungle is a mess for Labour

indicators.note: done awfully, the letters are badly arranged and mixed up

explanation.surface: A clumsy Labour Party mishandling leaves things in chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour' looks like the British political party, but it is one of the twelve labours of Hercules.
explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning the filthy stables of King Augeas was a task of Hercules, and the phrase now means a huge mess.

clue.text: He's concerned with being satisfied by a doctor

parts.note: to meet demands is to satisfy them
a physician is a doctor

explanation.surface: A man with a doctor who is concerned with being satisfied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' looks like part of 'being satisfied', but it is existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A philosopher of ontology studies the nature of existence and reality.

clue.text: Defaced drinking vessel, smashed on edge

indicators.note: with its face (front) taken off, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: a cup is a vessel for drinking from
smashed and tight are both slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A vandalised cup has been broken against a rim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smashed' looks like part of the vandal's picture, but it means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: someone tense and nervous is anxious or on edge.

clue.text: Artist to sketch undesirable existence

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist
to trace is to sketch or outline

explanation.surface: A painter is drawing a life nobody would want.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for the competitive daily grind of working life, a lifestyle nobody would choose.

clue.text: Ban text title out of Times

indicators.note: the letters named are taken out of the words before them

parts.note: T stands for time, so Times are several Ts, here every T in the phrase

explanation.surface: An instruction to remove a headline from The Times newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Times' looks like the newspaper, but it means Ts: remove all four Ts from TEXT TITLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as verbs: to exile someone is to banish them from their country.

clue.text: Order soldiers to stop endless festivity

indicators.note: to stop a gap is to plug it, so one piece goes inside the other
without its end, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a carnival is a festivity
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A command for troops to break up a party that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' looks like a command, but it is the biological rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxonomic term: the meat-eating mammals form a biological order.

clue.text: Famous number by '50s rocker

parts.note: a Teddy boy, or Ted, was a British youth of the 1950s rock and roll scene

explanation.surface: A well-known song by a 1950s rock and roller.
explanation.walkthrough: Teddy boys were 1950s British youths in Edwardian-style suits who loved rock and roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a celebrated person is well known or distinguished.

clue.text: Demands to settle on silly Scottish hill

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece settling on another sits above it

parts.note: to dun is to demand payment
inane means silly

explanation.surface: Requests to agree on a foolish Scottish hill.
explanation.walkthrough: This is the hill in Macbeth, near Perth in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a hill in the Sidlaws in Perthshire, famed from Macbeth.

clue.text: Error probed by philosopher, a blessing perhaps

indicators.note: a thing probed has something pushed into it, so the second part goes inside

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
John Stuart Mill was a philosopher

explanation.surface: A philosopher pokes at a mistake, which turns out to be a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic invocation 'in the name of God' is said as a blessing before acts, an example of one.

clue.text: Might one interest better author?

definitions.meaning: a bookie takes the bets of a gambler, a better, and might tempt them
someone who writes a book is its creator

explanation.surface: Could a writer be of more interest?
explanation.walkthrough: 'better' is one who bets, not 'more good'.
explanation.definitionFit: A turf accountant takes bets; literally, an author makes a book.

clue.text: Showing muscle, topless fashion in American battle scene

indicators.note: without its top, in a down entry the word loses its first letter

parts.note: flexing is showing off muscles
ton is an old word for fashion

explanation.surface: A bare-chested bodybuilder poses in an American setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' looks like a state of undress; it deletes the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Massachusetts town where the American Revolutionary War opened in 1775.

clue.text: Cruel newbie setters overwhelming girl

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the outer pieces surround another

parts.note: a tyro is a beginner
Ann is a girl's name
the setters speaking of themselves would say us

explanation.surface: Novice crossword setters harshly swamp a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a despotic, oppressive ruler is harsh and cruel.

clue.text: Short, unsexy jockeys bond

indicators.note: to jockey is to manoeuvre and shift about, so the letters are rearranged
cut short, the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: Small, unattractive riders connect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' loses the Y of 'unsexy', and 'jockeys' rearranges UNSEX.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a nexus is a connection or link between things.

clue.text: Roll back the Spanish writing: it's a sort of font

parts.note: a bap is a British bread roll

indicators.note: going back means these pieces are read from right to left

parts.note: la is a Spanish word for the
MS is a manuscript, a piece of writing
gives IT, the 's linking to the definition

explanation.surface: A typographer's quip about a style of type and a Spanish bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses LAMSIT to TISMAL. 'Font' looks like typography; it is the basin used in church christenings.
explanation.definitionFit: A church font holding water for christening is described with this adjective, so it is a kind of font.

clue.text: Knock over Sikh, half-cut Indian believer

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the word is turned upwards

parts.note: a rap is a knock

indicators.note: half-cut means only the first half of the word is kept

explanation.surface: A drunken Sikh is knocked over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' looks like drunk, but it halves 'Sikh'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Zoroastrian in India descended from Persian refugees.

clue.text: Back away from crazy American place

indicators.note: the back letter goes away from the word, removing its end

parts.note: loco is slang for crazy
US means American

explanation.surface: Retreat from a deranged American location.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a locus is a position or site where something happens.

clue.text: Alarm call all ignored: I sleep, turning over

indicators.note: turning over means the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep

indicators.note: the words named are left out, ignored, of the word before

explanation.surface: Someone sleeps through an alarm call, rolling over in bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: sudden fear and fright can be called alarm.

clue.text: Dig around radioactive metal that's sticking out

indicators.note: around means the dig surrounds the metal

parts.note: a dig is a poke or prod
U is the symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: Excavate round a radioactive metal that protrudes.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something protruding stands proud of a surface.

clue.text: Set aside weapon stocked by English vessel

indicators.note: stocked by means the weapon is held inside the other pieces

parts.note: an ark is a ship or vessel
an arm is a weapon

explanation.surface: A gun has been stored on an English ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: to reserve funds for a purpose is to allocate or reserve them.

clue.text: Spies gathering nothing in desert country

indicators.note: to gather something is to enclose it, so the spies surround the rest

parts.note: the CIA is the US spy agency

indicators.note: in means the nought goes inside the next word

parts.note: to rat is to desert or betray
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Secret agents collect nothing in an arid nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' looks like a noun describing the country, but it is the verb, to rat.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a Balkan state on the Adriatic is one nation.

clue.text: Politician failing to offer wrapping papers

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing

indicators.note: to wrap is to surround, so the offer goes round the papers

parts.note: to present is to offer
ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A politician fails to provide gift wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a deputy head of state is one kind of politician.
